question: A 39-year-old woman presents to her gynecologist for a routine visit. She has no complaints during this visit. She had an abnormal pap test 6 years ago that showed atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance. The sample was negative for human papillomavirus. On her follow-up Pap test 3 years later, there was no abnormality. The latest pap test results show atypical glandular cells with reactive changes in the cervical epithelium. The gynecologist decides to perform a colposcopy, and some changes are noted in this study of the cervical epithelium. The biopsy shows dysplastic changes in the epithelial cells. Which of the following is the next best step in the management of this patient?

options.opc: Follow-up pap smear in one year

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Atypical glandular cells" -> "Dysplastic changes on biopsy" -> "High suspicion for precancerous lesion" -> "Need for excisional procedure" -> "Loop electrosurgical excision procedure" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Atypical glandular cells" -> "Dysplastic changes on biopsy" -> "Potential for high-grade lesion" -> "Need for definitive diagnosis and treatment" -> "Cold knife conization" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Atypical glandular cells" -> "Dysplastic changes on biopsy" -> "Reactive changes" -> "Possible low-grade lesion" -> "Repeat colposcopy in 6 months" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Atypical glandular cells" -> "Dysplastic changes on biopsy" -> "Uncertain progression" -> "Monitor for changes" -> "Follow-up pap smear in one year" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Atypical glandular cells" -> "Dysplastic changes on biopsy" -> "Reactive changes" -> "Low suspicion for immediate progression" -> "Follow-up pap smear in 3 years" -> 40%
analysis: The patient has atypical glandular cells with dysplastic changes noted on biopsy. This suggests a higher risk of significant cervical pathology, such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) or even early invasive cancer. In such cases, a more definitive diagnostic and therapeutic procedure is warranted. A loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) is often recommended to both diagnose and treat high-grade cervical lesions. It allows for the removal of the transformation zone and any dysplastic tissue, providing both treatment and a specimen for further histological examination.
